shared_elements: shallow relief curvilinear motifs cut into stone
schematic outline designs without interior infill
justification: Both surfaces carry schematic, outline-only curvilinear relief carvings built from rings/discs and paired crescent arcs, a reasonably specific shared vocabulary, and in each case the motifs are combined into clustered compound designs rather than isolated signs. The biggest difference is organisation and support: A spreads its motifs freely and repetitively over irregular boulder faces with face-like heads, whereas B arranges its rings, arcs and a horizontal belt-like band in an ordered vertical scheme on the back of a human figure, a relationship (motifs applied to a body) that has no counterpart in A.
